item.description: arXiv:2611.06568v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Parrondo's paradox describes a surprising phenomenon in which certain combinations of biased quantum walks result in an unexpected reversal of their bias direction. To date, research on this effect has predominantly focused on one-dimensional discrete-time quantum walks that employ fixed sequences of two or three quantum coins, paired with a single shift operator. In this work, we first introduce a wide class of unitary shift operators which allow for three movement options (left, right or stay in place) of a walker in one time step, and we then demonstrate that Parrondo's paradox can also arise with a single coin and three distinct shift operators. Furthermore, we investigate how this paradox influences the time evolution of quantum entanglement between the walker and the coin in such quantum walks.
item.dc:creator: Zbigniew Walczak, Jaros{\l}aw H. Bauer

item.title: Equivalence of Correlated Catalytic and Marginal Asymptotic Transformations in Quantum Resource Theories
item.description: arXiv:2611.06573v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that correlated-catalytic state conversion is possible if and only if the marginal asymptotic conversion rate is at least one. Under general operational assumptions, this equivalence holds for arbitrary states in broad classes of entanglement, coherence, and magic theories. It reduces the characterization of correlated-catalytic convertibility to the computation of marginal asymptotic rates, and yields transitivity and equality of catalytic and marginal conversion rates. Under local operations and classical communication, we fully characterize correlated-catalytic conversion from arbitrary bipartite states to entangled pure states in terms of distillable entanglement. We show that correlated catalysts cannot increase the distillable entanglement or distillable secret key of any bipartite state, and in particular cannot make bound entanglement distillable. Extending our construction to adaptive communication protocols, we further prove that correlated catalysts cannot enhance the two-way private-state generation capacity of any finite-dimensional quantum channel.
item.dc:creator: Jingsong Ao, Aby Philip, Alexander Streltsov

item.title: Compatibility of Pauli Observables
item.description: arXiv:2611.06592v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Given an arbitrary finite family of Pauli observables, how sharply can they be approximated by a single measurement? We derive an exact state-space correspondence that characterises the resulting sharpness tradeoffs, establishing a link between incompatibility and preparation uncertainty. In particular, suitable ensembles of quantum states determine the full compatibility region and generate explicit parent measurements through Pauli conjugation and classical randomisation. The compatibility region depends only on the anti-commutativity graph and determines all nonuniform tradeoffs under standard noise models, including depolarising, probabilistic and generalised noise. We show that optimal sharpness tradeoffs are determined by spectral problems for signed Pauli Hamiltonians, whose ground states supply the seeds for optimal parent measurements. The correspondence also shows that magic is necessary to attain the full compatibility region of every noncommuting Pauli family. We quantify the resulting sharpness advantage and relate it to the reduced robustness of magic. Finally, we apply the framework to several structured Pauli families, obtaining exact compatibility characterisations and explicit optimal parents.
item.dc:creator: Daniel McNulty, Paolo Facchi, Saverio Pascazio

item.title: Discovering correlated error mechanisms: data-driven augmentation of detector error models improving decoding
item.description: arXiv:2611.06605v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Accurate decoder priors are essential for high-performance quantum error correction. Theoretical noise models inevitably omit physically relevant error mechanisms, most notably correlated errors, which appear consistently in experimental error budgets yet are absent from standard models. We introduce a data-driven method for augmenting detector error models (DEMs) by discovering entirely new error mechanisms directly from experimental detector-firing statistics, going beyond most existing approaches that merely refine the probabilities of already-known mechanisms. Our method generates candidates by combining pairs of existing mechanisms as building blocks, then filters and validates them using pairwise and higher-order detector correlations. Crucially, this construction provides each newly discovered mechanism with a well-defined logical effect derived from the constituent error mechanisms, enabling its direct use in decoding. Furthermore, each mechanism is accompanied by a natural decomposition into lower-order components, preserving compatibility with the original decoder. This is particularly valuable in settings that rely on correlated graph-based decoders such as correlated matching. We evaluate the method on surface-code simulations with correlated noise and correlated-matching decoding, demonstrating that, in a realistic near-term noise scenario, DEM augmentation increases the Lambda parameter by 20% across code distances 7-15 and reduces the logical error rate by 75% at code distance 15 relative to the unaugmented DEM. On experimental data from Google's superconducting device, the augmented DEM increases the Lambda parameter by 9% across code distances 5-7 and yields a reduction of 14% in logical error rate over the baseline for distance 7. To our knowledge, this is the first data-driven DEM augmentation method that produces decomposed hyperedges with assigned logical effects.
item.dc:creator: Zohar Schwartzman-Nowik, Matthew P. Stafford, Boris M. Varbanov, Joan Camps

item.title: Noise-regularized training of quantum circuit Born machines under a finite shot budget
item.description: arXiv:2611.06630v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum circuit Born machines (QCBMs) can learn distributions that are hard to sample from classically, but their value depends on generalizing from finite training data. Here, we study how hardware noise affects this generalization. We show that, for any noise process, the generalization gap of a QCBM trained with the maximum mean discrepancy is bounded by the complexity of the distributions the noisy model can reach. Scrambled local Pauli noise contracts this complexity but biases the model towards the uniform distribution, so residual noise acts as a regularizer whose optimal strength can be intermediate. We propose GENIE, a framework that realizes a chosen noise level with capped error mitigation and selects it during training from held-out data within a fixed execution budget, with provably bounded regret. In simulations on synthetic and census data, GENIE stays close to the best of four noise-control strategies, whereas every fixed noise level falls short in many settings.
item.dc:creator: Hoang M. Ngo, Quan Nguyen, Jung Taek Seo, Wanli Xing, My T. Thai

item.title: Precision Limits and Non-Gaussian Advantage in Optical Phase Estimation under Preparation Constraints
item.description: arXiv:2611.06645v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In optical quantum metrology, the scaling of the quantum Fisher information (QFI) with the mean photon number is a standard benchmark for relating precision to probe resources. For phase estimation, Heisenberg scaling corresponds to a quadratic growth of the QFI with the mean photon number, which Gaussian probes can approach. Interestingly, certain non-Gaussian probes can exhibit arbitrarily large QFI even at fixed mean photon number. Here, we clarify the resource requirements underlying this behavior by introducing a constraint that separates physically admissible states from inadmissible ones: an envelope on the photon-number distribution that arises naturally from the physical limitations of state-generation methods. Building on this constraint and considering pure single-mode probes, we define a resource quantity, $N_\mathrm{RMS}$, fixed by the preparation constraints, and derive a finite bound on the QFI whose Heisenberg scaling is attainable. We identify a genuine metrological advantage of non-Gaussian states over Gaussian probes subject to the same constraints. Finally, we illustrate these results with an optical preparation model based on a universal gate set.
item.dc:creator: V\'ictor Izquierdo, Javier Lalueza-Pu\'ertolas

item.title: Efficient quantum ultraspherical transform and a well-conditioned quantum spectral method
item.description: arXiv:2611.06651v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Solving differential equations is a promising application of quantum computing. Spectral methods, where the solution is represented by coefficients in a basis, are particularly well suited to quantum solvers because their structured discretizations can enable efficient linear-algebra operations while providing rapid convergence. Their quantum implementation, however, requires an efficient transform between amplitudes encoding function values and amplitudes encoding expansion coefficients. This work develops two key components of a quantum spectral method. First, we construct the quantum ultraspherical transform (QUT) for orthonormal ultraspherical polynomials, a basis that supports sparse and well-conditioned discretizations of differential equations. For the basis parameters $m=0$ and $1$, this transform reduces to the discrete cosine and sine transforms with known efficient circuits. Our contribution covers every fixed integer $m\geq2$: for dimensions $N$ with $N+m=2^n$, where $n$ is the number of qubits, the QUT achieves error at most $\varepsilon$ using a gate count polynomial in $n$ and $\log(1/\varepsilon)$. The construction builds on the quantum Fourier transform, augmented by approximations whose accuracy guarantees are independent of $N$. Second, we develop a quantum spectral solver for regular linear ordinary differential equations based on the QUT. Under suitable boundary conditions and data-access assumptions, preconditioning keeps condition numbers bounded independently of the basis size, allowing the solution state to be prepared at polylogarithmic cost in system size and inverse error. Together, these contributions provide a framework for quantum spectral methods with the potential to solve linear differential equations efficiently.
item.dc:creator: Trong Duong, Norbert Hosters

item.title: Flux Crosstalk Calibration from Zero Knowledge to High Precision in Fully Tunable Superconducting Circuits
item.description: arXiv:2611.06656v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Precise and independent flux control is essential for scalable superconducting processors built from frequency-tunable qubits and couplers, but flux crosstalk undermines it. Conventional calibration methods rely either on dedicated readout channels, which tunable couplers typically lack, or on readout schemes requiring extensive prior spectroscopy of the qubit and coupler. We demonstrate two independent methods that characterize coupler flux crosstalk without directly driving or measuring the couplers. The first method is zero-knowledge characterization, which exploits intrinsic coupler-resonator coupling to yield rapid and accurate estimates with no prior qubit or coupler spectroscopy, accelerating large scale bring-up. The second method is symmetric branch cancellation, which isolates crosstalk from other dispersive effects allowing for quantifying with high precision. Combined with an improved iterative procedure, these methods suppress residual coupler crosstalk below $5\times10^{-5}$, providing a complete route from zero-knowledge initialization to high-precision crosstalk characterization in fully tunable architectures.
item.dc:creator: Y. Gao, A. Galicia, J. R. Guimar\~aes, Y. Haddad, Y. Liu, J. Cereijo, D. A. Volkov, H. Bhardwaj, M. Neis, M. Jerger, P. A. Bushev, R. Barends

item.title: Experimental activation of hidden metrological steerability in quantum channels via stochastic filtering
item.description: arXiv:2611.06668v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum steering-assisted metrology allows a trusted party (Bob) to improve local phase estimation by exploiting classical information communicated by an untrusted party (Alice). In realistic scenarios, however, the channel is subject to noise that degrades steerability and suppresses the associated metrological advantage. Here, we demonstrate that stochastic pre- and post-filtering operations can revive the violation of the metrological steering inequality (MSI) in phase-covariant amplitude-damping channels where it is initially absent, thereby activating a hidden metrological steerability and restoring their usefulness for quantum metrology. Specifically, the critical damping parameter beyond which the MSI violation is suppressed is raised from $\gamma_c \approx 0.5$ to $\gamma_c \approx 0.75$ for the largest filter strength considered. We verify this in a photonic experiment, where polarization qubits carrying the encoded phase are transmitted through an amplitude-damping channel implemented with a two-path Sagnac interferometer, and the stochastic operations are realized with glass plates at the Brewster angle. By tuning the filter strength and scanning the damping parameter over its full range, we observe the revival of the MSI violation, obtained at the cost of a reduced success probability inherent to the stochastic nature of the filtering operations. Our results establish that metrological utility and steerability can be activated through stochastic operations even when these properties are absent in the original noisy channel, extending filtering-based activation from witnesses of nonclassicality to a certified and operationally quantified metrological advantage.
item.dc:creator: H. S. Karthik, J. Berm\'udez, D. Montoya, J. Parra-Past\'en, F. M. Quinteros, Akshata Shenoy H., M. Paw{\l}owski, S. P. Walborn, G. Lima, E. S. G\'omez

item.title: QASPA-MaxCut on Unweighted Graphs: Edge Encoding and QAOA Restarts
item.description: arXiv:2611.06698v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Max-Cut is a common testbed for near-term quantum optimization because it has a simple Ising Hamiltonian, established classical baselines, and a parameterized quantum circuit whose performance depends on the outer classical optimizer. This paper develops QASPA-MaxCut, a shift-phase circuit for Max-Cut that encodes graph edges through controlled $R_y$ rotations of the form $\mathrm{CX}_{ij}R_y(\theta_{ij})\mathrm{CX}_{ij}$. We derive the exact two-qubit algebra of the edge block, trace an unweighted four-vertex example, and compare one-layer QASPA-MaxCut with depth-one QAOA by exact state-vector simulation. The protocol uses seed 42, evaluates connected backbone-augmented random graphs with additional-edge probabilities $p_{\mathrm{edge}}\in\{0.1,0.3,0.5,0.7\}$, and adds nineteen custom unweighted topologies. The QASPA-MaxCut score is reported after the algorithm's classical selection stage: the four leading QASPA bit strings are evaluated by the Max-Cut objective, and the best cut is retained. The QAOA score is the expected approximation ratio after local optimization, reported as a best-of-$k$ curve over one to ten restarts. In these small exact simulations, fixed-angle QASPA-MaxCut produces reported group-mean selection ratios between $0.955$ and $1.000$, the topology-level readout is unchanged in the retained finite-shot checks under the rule $\lceil 0.03047\cdot 2^n+1016.2\rceil$, and depth-one QAOA improves with additional classical restarts while remaining lower than the QASPA selection score in the reported mean summaries. This comparison motivates further study of the classical search budget needed to obtain competitive Max-Cut samples at shallow circuit depth.
item.dc:creator: Dmytro Sapozhnyk

item.title: Phase-Locked Quantum Battery Charging via Dissipative Mode Selection
item.description: arXiv:2611.06712v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate how dynamical instability and reservoir engineering can be harnessed to enhance the quality of quantum-battery charging in a bosonic two-mode system. We show that reservoir-engineered dissipative coupling selectively amplifies a single unstable quasi-dark mode, enabling phase-locked exponential charging at a reduced gain threshold, whereas coherent coupling can amplify two frequency-split unstable modes, resulting in persistent beating. This dissipative mode selection yields a near-unit ergotropy fraction and a substantially higher work-like signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), defined as ergotropy divided by the standard deviation of battery energy. Although optimizing the driving frequency enables coherent coupling to achieve faster charging and higher ergotropy power, dissipative coupling retains its advantage in the work-like SNR. An exact finite-time source-noise relation reveals that this advantage arises from a more constructive accumulation of coherent driving relative to incoherent fluctuations. Our results establish dissipative mode selection as a promising route to high-quality quantum-battery charging.
item.dc:creator: Borhan Ahmadi, Lei Du, Andr\'e H. A. Malavazi, Shabir Barzanjeh, Adam Miranowicz, Pawe{\l} Horodecki

item.title: Solving a non-abelian hidden subgroup problem on a trapped-ion quantum computer: the power of the measurement basis
item.description: arXiv:2611.06716v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The hidden subgroup problem (HSP) unifies many of the best-known quantum speed-ups. For abelian groups it is solved efficiently by weak Fourier sampling, but for non-abelian groups, which include the cases relevant to graph isomorphism and lattice-based cryptography, the right measurement basis is crucial and often unknown. We experimentally study the HSP over the $q$-hedral groups $\mathbb{Z}_q \ltimes \mathbb{Z}_p$, which interpolate between the dihedral and affine groups and mark a boundary between instances that are efficiently solvable and those that are only information-theoretically solvable. On the IonQ Forte trapped-ion quantum computer, with $p \le 7$, we implement weak Fourier sampling, strong Fourier sampling in an adapted basis, strong Fourier sampling of adjacent pairs, and forgetful abelian sampling. We demonstrate that the theoretical predictions of Moore, Rockmore, Russell and Schulman survive on a noisy device: weak sampling reveals nothing about the hidden subgroup, the adapted basis succeeds for large $q$, adjacent pairs succeed for small $q$, and forgetful sampling saturates below unit success. For $p=7$, $q=6$, the hardware exceeds the success probability of an exhaustively optimised classical algorithm for up to three oracle queries.
item.dc:creator: Oliver O'Brien

item.title: A Quantum Lower Bound for Triangle Finding
item.description: arXiv:2611.06751v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Triangle finding is a fundamental problem in graph theory that has played a central role in the development of quantum algorithmic techniques. For $N$-vertex graphs given by their adjacency matrices, a long line of work has improved the quantum query upper bound from $O(N^{3/2})$ to $O(N^{5/4})$. However, the best known lower bound has remained the elementary $\Omega(N)$ bound obtained from unstructured search. We prove the first superlinear quantum query lower bound for triangle finding, showing that $\Omega(N^{13/12})$ queries are necessary. Our result also implies the same lower bound for triangle detection and for detecting every fixed connected non-bipartite graph. The proof builds on the compressed oracle approach of Zhandry and the transfer approaches of Belovs. It compares the computation on graphs with a planted triangle to the computation on random graphs conditioned to be triangle-free, through a map on the input registers that almost commutes with every query. We average over local changes to the input while preserving its distribution, through a procedure known as conditional resampling. Our main technical contribution is a set of estimates that let us control the query error under this averaging, despite the dependence introduced by conditioning a dense graph to be triangle-free.
item.dc:creator: Arjan Cornelissen, Amin Shiraz Gilani, Xingyu Zhou

item.title: Near-Quantum-Limited Readout for the Princeton Axion Search using a sub-GHz Kinetic Inductance Traveling Wave Parametric Amplifier
item.description: arXiv:2611.06761v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Parametric amplifiers are a workhorse for near-quantum-limited measurements above 1 GHz. However, amplifier development has been more limited below 1 GHz. We present a kinetic inductance traveling-wave parametric amplifier (KI-TWPA) operating over 300-700 MHz, with gain exceeding 30 dB and pump powers of a few hundred nanowatts. The system noise performance, as measured by a variable-temperature noise source, is 2.5-3.5 quanta. This device is a versatile new tool for precision measurements of sub-GHz signals, with applications including readout of semiconductor spin qubits, superconducting detector arrays, and searches for new physics beyond the Standard Model. We characterize aspects of the amplifier performance relevant to axion searches, including gain drift, compression point, amplifier noise at various operating temperatures, readout with an input circulator, and magnetic field insensitivity.
item.dc:creator: Joe Wiedemann, Roman Kolevatov, Jianyang Fu, Joelle-Marie Begin, Nate Otto, Felix St-Amour, Lyman Page, Henry LeDuc, Peter Day, Saptarshi Chaudhuri

item.title: Non-compact Kogut-Susskind gauge theories: 1D lattice models with exact ${\rm SL}(2,\mathbb{R})$ gauge invariance
item.description: arXiv:2611.06771v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Kogut-Susskind (KS) formulation of gauge theories constructs quantum many-body Hamiltonians with gauge invariance under a compact Lie group exactly implemented on a spatial lattice. Here, we revisit this construction for a non-compact gauge group. Although motivated in part by theories like general relativity whose first-order formulation involves the non-compact Lorentz group as a local symmetry, we focus on simpler cases in one spatial dimension akin to the Schwinger model. In a bottom-up approach, we show how exact gauge invariance under the simplest non-compact Lie group ${\rm SL}(2,\mathbb{R})$ can be retained exactly on a 1D lattice, and highlight the differences that arise with respect to compact gauge groups, including a continuous spectrum of the Casimir operators of the gauge fields and the emergence of infinite-dimensional representations of the matter fields. For the pure gauge theory, we discuss how a consistent restriction to the positive semigroup ${\rm SL}^{+}(2,\mathbb{R})$ reproduces well-known results from the quantization of Jackiw-Teitelboim (JT) gravity. Motivated by the constraint structure of general dilaton gravity, we introduce static charges coupled to the non-compact gauge field, which can be realised by single-fermion degrees of freedom living in an additional, synthetic dimension. With static charges our lattice model remains exactly integrable, but when extending to dynamical fermionic matter, we arrive at an interacting 1D ${\rm SL}(2,\mathbb{R})$ KS gauge theory. We give an interpretation of this model as a chain of charges sequentially connected by strings whose tension pulls matter left or right depending on the sign of the relative continuous ${\rm SL}(2,\mathbb{R})$ fluxes. This picture becomes exact when the involved ${\rm SL}(2,\mathbb{R})$ charges are strongly self-interacting, where we solve the reduced two-body problem analytically.
item.dc:creator: Carlos Fulgado-Claudio, Torsten V. Zache

item.title: Entanglement Entropy in Non Relativistic Collisions
item.description: arXiv:2611.06774v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study numerically the build-up of entanglement entropy between two colliding, non relativistic particles, that are driven by the plain Schr\"odinger equation containing local, finite range potentials, and whose initial state is the product of two independent wave packets. Different situations are considered, ranging from a tunnel and mirror effect at low energy in front of a barrier, to higher energies, and also attraction rather than repulsion. While the calculated wave functions and density matrices significantly depend on the physical situations described by our models, the build-up trends and values in time of entanglement entropy look surprisingly alike one another.
item.dc:creator: Bertrand Giraud (IPhT Saclay), Robi Peschanski (IPhT Saclay)

item.title: Resource-efficient formulations of the Knapsack problem for quantum computing
item.description: arXiv:2611.06797v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum computing has emerged as a new tool for solving combinatorial optimization problems. Quantum optimization approaches usually operate on the subclass of Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization (QUBO) problems. Many optimization problems can be reformulated in this form, though there are often multiple ways to do so. The choice of formulation can considerably affect the performance of QUBO solvers in practice. In this work, we study QUBO formulations of the Knapsack problem, a canonical example of a problem with inequality constraints. In the standard formulation these constraints are converted into penalty terms, which requires additional slack variables. Here, we investigate three more resource-efficient approaches for formulating the Knapsack as a QUBO. The first two modify the standard formulation, either by deriving a smaller penalty constant or by reducing the number of slack variables. The third approach is a wholly different method, which avoids the use of slack variables entirely. All three approaches increase the probability of finding the optimal solution, both in simulations of the linear ramp Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (LR-QAOA) and on a D-Wave quantum annealer. The slackless method performs best, increasing success probabilities by several orders of magnitude even for relatively small problem sizes.
item.dc:creator: Pim van den Heuvel, Vrinda Mehta, Dennis Willsch, J. A. Montanez-Barrera, Kristel Michielsen

item.title: Finite-temperature transition-window weights on a fault-tolerant quantum computer: duplex filtering on a thermal purification
item.description: arXiv:2611.06809v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The excite-filter-readout framework of Kharazi et al. computes zero-temperature response windows on a fault-tolerant quantum computer from a pure ground state. We extend it to Gibbs states, where the two objects decouple: filters act on absolute energies, a thermal response on transition frequencies. The extension rests on a Liouville-space/TFD identity, explicit in the block-encoding/QSP setting: the thermally weighted transition-window weight is a spectral projection of H_0 (x) I - I (x) H_0^T onto the Schmidt (thermofield-double) purification, instance of Rall's framework. Around it we assemble a routed-SELECT block encoding (one Hamiltonian query per filter query), a conjugate-pair readout, and a four-route (duplex, bin, Fourier-LCU, METTS) compatibility analysis. The cost is multiplicative and conditional: a per-window query bound M_"AE" * (2*sqrt(d/Z_"lb")*d_"vt" + 4*d_W), with a tight signal-adaptive count, the optimal sqrt(alpha beta) degree, and a window-edge term. The preparation factor sqrt(d/Z) grows exponentially with system size at fixed temperature in positive-entropy-density systems (2.08 -> 25.7, N = 8 to 14 at beta = 2), relieved only as beta -> 0. Zero temperature is recovered for beta G >= ln(2(d-1)||D||^2/epsilon). Identities are cross-checked between independent formula paths to 10^(-16)-10^(-12) and the readout assembly is validated at matrix level under a block-encoding promise.
item.dc:creator: Yujin Tang, Yunlong Liu, Miao Xu, Qing-Xing Xie

item.title: Linear-time erasure recovery for quantum expander codes
item.description: arXiv:2611.06818v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Erasures are used to model faults at a subset of known locations in various platforms used to construct fault-tolerant quantum computers. Beyond the utility in erasure recovery, efficient decoders for erasures are useful to both understand error decoders and as a subroutine for error decoding. Classical expander codes, which belong to the family of low-density parity-check (LDPC) codes, can be equipped with the Peeling decoder which works in linear time. Our main result is the algorithm Small-Set-Peeling, a quantum generalization of the classical Peeling decoder for erasures, that applies to quantum expander codes (Tillich, Z\'emor, IEEE T-IT 2013; Leverrier, Tillich, Z\'emor, FOCS 2015). This decoder can correct up to $D-1$ erasures, where $D$ is the (design) distance of the code and, importantly, is the first decoder that is guaranteed to do so in linear time. Combining with the erasure-conversion algorithm Small-Set-Find (Krishna, Livni-Navon, Wootters, SODA 2024), our result also implies the existence of a novel graph-local linear-time decoder for Pauli errors.
item.dc:creator: Anirudh Krishna, Christopher A. Pattison

item.title: GFlowQEC: Generative Flow Networks that Learn to Sample Quantum LDPC Codes
item.description: arXiv:2611.06819v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Choosing a quantum error-correcting code for a real device means scoring candidates with circuit-level simulations so slow that only a few hundred can be run. So every evaluation counts, and a search is judged by how many good codes it finds per paid evaluation. Quantum LDPC codes built from a few group elements protect many logical qubits, but good ones are rare in a huge space. We introduce GFlowQEC, to our knowledge the first generative flow network (GFlowNet) for quantum code design. It builds a code one group element at a time and learns to propose codes in proportion to a power of their score. We train it once on scores from earlier searches, freeze it, and let it propose lifted-product codes with 180 physical qubits, scored by their distances. Ranking ten of its draws per paid call, it finds more than twice as many new top-scoring codes (inequivalent to any it was trained on) as tuned parallel tempering, even when tempering starts from GFlowQEC's training codes. It finds more than three and a half times as many as a supervised screen ranking ten random candidates per call. When both rank a hundred, the screen beats GFlowQEC, and does best ranking GFlowQEC's draws. Soft Q-learning, which shares the GFlowNet's optimal policy, does as well at one noise bias and better at the other, so the gain does not depend on the GFlowNet's training loss. Trained proposers can make a budget of expensive evaluations go further when good codes are rare.
item.dc:creator: Nuno Batista, Gabriel Falcao, Penousal Machado

item.title: Quantum Algorithms for Molecular Response Functions: Resolvent Kernels, Time-Domain Sampling, Query Lower Bounds with Matched Single-Point Calibers, and a Six-Route Comparison
item.description: arXiv:2611.06821v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum algorithms for molecular response functions have mostly been studied one route at a time, most prominently the indicator-binning algorithm of Kharazi et al. We compare six routes within one accounting framework and state the conversions between their resource calibers. On the resolvent route the Lorentz-broadened spectrum is exactly a resolvent expectation; at finite gamma two boundary terms, a reversal term and a permanent-dipole pseudo-line, enter a disjoint error budget. Because the kernel subnormalization is exactly 1, the published binning accounting carries a removable Theta(alpha+1+omega) factor (49.69x and 7.75x at the definitional caliber), a correction that applies to both routes. Estimating the square root of the kernel amplitude lowers the readout cost from beta^2/mu_tilde_2 to beta/sqrt(mu_tilde_2). On the time-domain route we prove a single-point amplitude-estimation theorem and convert the generalized QPE of Loaiza et al. to the same accounting. The lower bounds are Theta_tilde(1/gamma) for parameter location, Theta(1/(gamma epsilon)) for windowed values, Omega(n/gamma) inside a restricted correlation-sampling class, and Omega(1/(epsilon gamma^2)) on the Lorentzian object; in the single-circuit-resolution caliber, gamma^(-n) is a grid-coverage artifact. Six routes, their calibers, an n=2 assembly with a component-grade coherence, and a phase diagram over the tested ensembles form one accounting map.
item.dc:creator: Yunlong Liu, Yujin Tang, Miao Xu, Qing-Xing Xie

item.title: Optimal Holding Times for Entanglement Swapping
item.description: arXiv:2611.06823v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We revisit the optimization of entanglement holding times in memory-based quantum repeaters for maximizing entanglement swapping throughput under different fidelity constraints - strict, probabilistic, and mean. We consider two heterogeneous quantum links that are equipped with single or multiple memories and differ in decoherence rates, memory capacities, entanglement attempt rates and success probabilities, as well as classical communication latencies. Efficient models are developed to estimate the expected entanglement throughput and the probability density functions of the conditional wait time to swap. The models are then used to satisfy different fidelity requirements by optimizing the maximum holding times for the two links. Finally, our proposed model and approach are validated with a discrete-event quantum network simulator.
item.dc:creator: Van Sy Mai, Richard J. La, Abdella Battou

item.title: Probing gravity at megahertz frequencies with levitated rotors
item.description: arXiv:2611.06893v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The near-field gravitational interaction between masses is always thought of as instantaneous, an assumption experimentally tested only up to 1.7 kHz, where measurements yield a bounds at the $10^{-5}$ s level. We propose a near-field experiment reaching up to megahertz frequencies, in which a levitated microrotor modulates a mass quadrupole and a second rotor measures the resulting gravitational tidal field as a torque. Because the detector rotor acts as a mechanical local oscillator, the megahertz signal is downconverted to a convenient band of a few hertz, and since at fixed geometry neither the torque nor the integration time depends on the rotation rate, higher frequencies are reached at no cost in sensitivity. With parameters within reach of magnetically levitated NdFeB rotors, a signal at 2 MHz yields a torque of $2\cdot 10^{-25}$ Nm, detectable in under an hour at 10 mK. Treating a possible departure from instantaneous gravitational coupling through a field relaxation time, the measured torque could constrain it at the $10^{-8}$ s level, improving on the existing bounds by more than three orders of magnitude. As a byproduct of our analysis, we derive the sensitivity of a rotor operated as a tunable high-frequency gravitational-wave detector, finding that a noise-equivalent strain around $10^{-22}$ Hz$^{-1/2}$ could be achievable in the megahertz band.
item.dc:creator: Matteo Fadel, Andrea Vinante

item.title: Arithmetic Depth, Minimal Gate Alphabets, and Exact Program-State Resources for Single-Qubit Dyadic Programs
item.description: arXiv:2611.06909v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Resource analyses for quantum programs commonly provide safe upper bounds on qubits, gates, or non-Clifford operations. We study a single-qubit dyadic fragment in which the deepest exact resource layer can instead be inferred exactly. Starting from the normalized-midpoint misty-state syntax, we define dyadic program states and the real cyclotomic tower $K_D=\mathbb Q(2\cos(\pi/2^D))$. For the projective single-qubit Clifford-cyclotomic tower $\widehat G_D\subseteq SO(3)$, we prove the relative intersection law $\widehat G_D\cap SO(3,K_d)=\widehat G_d$ for $d\le D$. Combining this descent theorem with an arithmetic-closure invariant for adaptive stabilizer processing yields $\mathrm{Fdepth}(U)=\mathrm{Adepth}(U)=\mathrm{Rdepth}(U)$: the smallest real cyclotomic field containing the Bloch matrix of an exactly synthesizable channel, the shallowest dyadic gate alphabet realizing it up to global phase, and the shallowest dyadic program-state layer sufficient for exact stabilizer-assisted implementation coincide. At that common minimum, known fixed-alphabet synthesis gives minimum primitive-rotation count. We package the result as an exact static resource effect and outline a certificate-producing compiler.
item.dc:creator: Tony Newton, Dan-Adrian German

item.title: Using topology to reveal all mutually unbiased bases in dimension six
item.description: arXiv:2611.06917v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Mutually unbiased bases (MUBs) describe complementary quantum measurements: certainty in one basis gives no information about the others. In dimension six, triples of MUBs are known, but whether a fourth basis could exist remained unresolved for over three decades. OpenAI recently reported a proof that none exists. Here we use the topology of the space of complex Hadamard matrices, which describe transitions between MUBs, to characterize all sets in dimension six. We prove that every mutually unbiased triple belongs to a two-parameter family or is a single isolated triple built from the Fourier matrix. Since none of them extend to a fourth basis, this also proves that no four MUBs exist. Our proof rests on a new topological result that all order-six complex Hadamard matrices except Tao's form a connected space. Connectedness reduces the classification of triples to finitely many overlapping four-dimensional phase balls. We certify with interval arithmetic that these balls cover the space and for every pair of MUBs represented in a ball, we then determine all third bases that extend it. Dimension six is now the first non-prime-power dimension in which all sets of MUBs are classified.
item.dc:creator: Mateo C\'ardenes Wuttig, Joseph Tindall

item.title: Cryptanalysis of Isogeny-Based Quantum Money with Rational Points
item.description: arXiv:2508.00351v2 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Quantum money is a representative application in cryptography that utilizes quantum technology to achieve security that is unattainable with classical systems. Since the theoretical proposal by Wiesner in 1983, the most recent instantiation is the quantum money using class group actions on elliptic curves, proposed by Montgomery and Sharif in Asiacrypt'24. In this work, we propose a concrete cryptanalysis by leveraging the efficiency of evaluating division polynomials with the coordinates of rational points, offering a speedup of $O(\log^4p)$ compared to the brute-force attack. While the resulting attack still runs in exponential time, our method provides the first nontrivial algorithmic insight into their structural hardness. Furthermore, due to the algebraic properties of rational points and quadratic twists, our technique naturally yields a more efficient verification procedure for the underlying quantum money. We believe this new line of analysis opens promising directions for future research in elliptic-curve-based quantum cryptography.
item.dc:creator: Hyeonhak Kim, Donghoe Heo, Seokhie Hong, Sangjin Lee, Suhri Kim

item.title: LaQX: A JAX Toolkit for Neural Quantum State Simulations of Lattice Quantum Many-Body Models
item.description: arXiv:2611.04333v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Neural quantum states provide accurate variational representations for interacting lattice fermions and spins. Turning a new ansatz into a reproducible calculation, however, requires coordinated implementations of the Hamiltonian, sampling, optimization, observables, and accelerator parallelism. We present LaQX (Lattice Quantum simulation based on jaX), an open-source neural quantum state library based on JAX that organizes these components through common functional interfaces. Beyond ground-state variational Monte Carlo, LaQX supports excited-state calculations, Green's Function Monte Carlo refinement, adiabatic evolution, and real-time evolution with time-dependent variational Monte Carlo. It consolidates methods developed in recent high-accuracy neural quantum state studies of the Hubbard model and frustrated magnets, and the package has been used to investigate the triangular-lattice Hofstadter-Hubbard model. We document these capabilities with reproducible calculations for Hubbard, $J_1$-$J_2$ Heisenberg, altermagnetic Hubbard, and interacting Hofstadter models. Function-oriented modules separate the scientific components and limit the source context needed for extensions by human developers and large language models. Source code, documentation, and executable examples are available at https://github.com/bytedance/laqx.
item.dc:creator: Yuntian Gu, Chaohui Fan, Ruichen Li, Haoxiang Chen, Weizhong Fu, Yixiao Chen, Dingshun Lv, Weiluo Ren, Tao Xiang, Liwei Wang, Mingpu Qin, Xiang Li

item.title: Estimating the generator of matrix exponential time-series
item.description: arXiv:2611.04521v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The achievable precision in estimating the spectrum of a time-series signal that is promised to be sparse in Fourier space deteriorates rapidly as the spectral peaks get closer together, as soon as we introduce noise. Here, we study the related task of generator estimation: estimating the generator of a matrix exponential time-series and its eigenvalues. We obtain rigorous non-asymptotic precision guarantees on genESPRIT, a practical algorithm solving generator estimation, and show that this task can be solved with precision independent of the spectral spacing. The guarantees are complemented by a Cram\'er--Rao analysis of a relaxation of the problem. In particular, in the case of unitary data with bounded additive noise with effective entrywise variance $\sigma^2$, we show that genESPRIT estimates the associated propagator matrix in Frobenius norm with precision scaling as $\tilde{\mathcal{O}}(\sigma NL^{-\frac12})$ in the length of the time-series $L$ and matrix dimension $N$, matching the corresponding spectrum-independent Cram\'er--Rao standard deviation scaling up to logarithmic factors. We prove that the matching distance error in the spectrum estimated by genESPRIT scales as $\tilde{\mathcal{O}} (\sigma^2 N^3 L^{-1} + \sigma N^{\frac32} L^{-\frac32} )$, which we compare to the lower bound on the corresponding Cram\'er--Rao bound with the asymptotic standard deviation scaling $\mathcal{O}(\sigma L^{-\frac32})$. These guarantees provide the first rigorous bounds on solving the generator estimation problem. As the matrix exponential time-series can be obtained from linearly independent vector time-series by concatenation, this work opens up a new direction in spectral estimation, which circumvents the problem of crowded spectra, under the additional assumption of linear independence.
item.dc:creator: Jon\'a\v{s} Fuksa, Jens Eisert, Ingo Roth

item.title: Photon-Counting Readout via Electro-Optic Microwave-to-Optical Transduction for Axion Haloscopes
item.description: arXiv:2611.05444v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Axion dark matter searches require highly sensitive detection schemes with high scan rate to efficiently explore the parameter space. Building upon the conventional Sikivie haloscope, where axions convert into microwave photons inside a magnetic-field-immersed resonant cavity, we present a photon-counting scheme based on an electro-optic microwave-to-optical transducer. Through a comprehensive theoretical model under realistic experimental constraints, we find that the optimal operating regime employs an overcoupled microwave cavity, trading peak transduction efficiency for reduced transducer noise. Furthermore, combining parameters already demonstrated in existing devices, in a device with optimized extrinsic coupling rates, would yield a scan-rate enhancement of 5-10 relative to quantum-limited homodyne detection. Improvements in quality factors, coupling rates, and thermal management push this enhancement beyond 50. While our quantitative model is benchmarked at 9 GHz, the scheme adapts well to haloscopes across the 5-12 GHz range, where shrinking cavity volumes severely degrade the achievable scan rate. These results demonstrate the potential of electro-optical photon detection as a high-speed detection technique for axion dark matter searches.
item.dc:creator: Jing Wu, Raphael Cervantes, Doga Murat Kurkcuoglu, Zheshen Zhang, Silvia Zorzetti

item.title: A Fully Polynomial Approximation Algorithm for the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick Model
item.description: arXiv:2611.05446v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Montanari's incremental approximate message passing (IAMP) algorithm [FOCS 2019; SIAM J. Comput., 2025] and the zero-temperature formulation of El Alaoui, Montanari and Sellke (AMS) [Ann. Probab., 2021] find a $(1-\varepsilon)$ approximation to the maximum Sherrington-Kirkpatrick (SK) energy in $C(\varepsilon)N^2$ operations for fixed accuracy, with probability tending to one as $N\to\infty$, under their respective full-support and access-model assumptions. However, it was unknown whether this approximation could be achieved with work polynomial in both $N$ and $1/\varepsilon$, together with quantitative guarantees at finite dimension. Under the same assumptions as AMS, we introduce grouped IAMP with exact Gaussian query outputs (GEG-IAMP), which is the first SK approximation algorithm with total work polynomial in $N$ and $1/\varepsilon$ and a finite-size guarantee above a dimension threshold polynomial in $1/\varepsilon$ and $\log(1/\alpha)$. More precisely, for every $\alpha\in(0,1/2)$, it returns a $(1-\varepsilon)$ approximation with probability at least $1-\alpha$ whenever $N\ge \mathsf{K}\varepsilon^{-2}\log^2(e/\varepsilon)\log(\mathsf{K}/\alpha)$, using $O(N^2/\varepsilon)$ work and $O(N^2)$ storage. GEG-IAMP replaces the Onsager correction by Reeves's coupling construction [arXiv:2508.10782] and groups Euler-Maruyama steps into $O(1/\varepsilon)$ matrix-vector products. We also prove a relative guarantee for AMS IAMP with $O(N^2\varepsilon^{-3}\log^2(e/\varepsilon))$ work but a sufficient dimension exponential in inverse accuracy. By returning a fixed configuration below its dimension threshold, GEG-IAMP also provides an asymptotic fully polynomial randomized approximation scheme (AFPRAS), with an additive error independent of dimension.
item.dc:creator: Dylan Herman, Shouvanik Chakrabarti, Junhyung Lyle Kim, Guneykan Ozgul

item.title: Superconducting Qubits as Quantum Targets for Direct Particle Scattering
item.description: arXiv:2611.05469v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce a novel approach to particle detection in which a superconducting qubit itself serves as the scattering target and a resolved transition between circuit eigenstates constitutes the observable final state. The scattering amplitude factorizes into the incident-particle current and a finite-momentum electromagnetic transition response of the qubit. This momentum dependence is essential in that the energy transfer is fixed by the microwave-scale level spacing, whereas a nonrelativistic incident particle can transfer a spatial momentum parametrically larger than that energy and thereby resolve the device geometry. For charge-dominated processes, we recast the response as an induced-offset-charge kernel obtained from an auxiliary electrostatic weighting potential, providing a practical route from circuit geometry to a differential scattering cross section. We illustrate the framework with an Xmon-style transmon and photon-mediated scattering of dark matter. The exceptionally small qubit transition threshold opens sensitivity to an eV-to-keV mass regime that is largely unexplored by existing direct-detection experiments.
item.dc:creator: Doojin Kim, Kyoungchul Kong, Myeonghun Park

item.title: Shapiro spikes in driven quantum fluids
item.description: arXiv:2611.05477v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Periodic driving of a Josephson junction produces resonant transport signatures known as Shapiro spikes, conventionally described by effective circuit models. Here, we demonstrate Shapiro spikes in a neutral quantum fluid using simulations of a potential-biased atomic Josephson junction. The dc-current resonances follow the expected Bessel-function scaling, including the suppression and revival of individual resonances with increasing modulation strength. We uncover their microscopic mechanism by showing that the phase-winding frequency develops finite plateaus at integer multiples of the drive frequency. These phase-locked states are sustained by quantized-vortex nucleation and the associated $2\pi$ phase slips. Remarkably, within a locking plateau, the dc current and density transfer can reverse direction while the phase-winding frequency remains locked to the drive, giving rise to negative-mobility transport. Our results establish a microscopic link between vortex-mediated phase slips, Shapiro resonances, and anomalous transport in a neutral quantum fluid, revealing how quantized vortices convert resonant transport into phase-locked dynamics with negative mobility.
item.dc:creator: Vijay Pal Singh, Ludwig Mathey, Luigi Amico

item.title: Stabiliser codes over prime fields as weighted graphs and as quantum sets of lines
item.description: arXiv:2611.05489v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We further develop the theory of quantum stabiliser codes and its links with graph theory and finite geometry. We prove that an [[n,k,d]]_p stabiliser code over a finite field with p elements, p prime, gives rise to a graph on n-k vertices together with two disjoint independent sets of size k. Its edges are weighted with elements of a finite field of size p. If k=0, such codes are known as graph states. Second, we view stabiliser codes as so-called quantum sets of lines in projective space, allowing us to determined their minimum distance geometrically. We describe two geometrical operations to obtain new quantum sets of lines from given quantum sets of lines. As an application, we list the number of stabiliser codes up to equivalence, for given small parameters.
item.dc:creator: Simeon Ball, G\"ulizar G\"unay, Robin Simoens, Ricard Vilar

item.title: Quantum computing for high energy nuclear physics
item.description: arXiv:2611.05491v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Quantum information science (QIS) offers a new set of conceptual and computational tools ideally suited to exploring the many-body, out-of-equilibrium, and real-time properties of strongly interacting quantum systems. These themes find a natural counterpart in high energy nuclear physics, whose central goal is to describe the properties of Quantum Chromodynamics (QCD), the theory of the strong interaction, under extreme conditions. Relevant examples range from the formation and internal structure of hadrons, to the collective and thermalization dynamics of strongly interacting QCD matter, and the properties of complex many-body scattering processes. Although tremendous progress has been made over the past decades in our understanding of QCD in the nuclear physics context, through perturbative methods, lattice QCD, and effective theory descriptions, phenomena that are intrinsically connected to real-time dynamics, highly entangled many-body evolution, or finite density regimes remain only partially accessible with existing approaches. In this article, we argue that QIS can help realize a new paradigm for addressing these open questions. With the aim of making the discussion accessible to both high energy nuclear physics and QIS audiences, we provide an overview of selected open problems in high energy nuclear physics, with emphasis on aspects motivated by collider phenomenology, and discuss how they can be approached using QIS tools. This connection is illustrated through representative examples drawn from the recent literature, making the case that QIS can become a driving force for discovery in nuclear physics in the coming years.
item.dc:creator: Jo\~{a}o Barata

item.title: Dynamical Signatures of Selective Gap Closing in Multi-Dimensional Monotone Quasiperiodic Operators
item.description: arXiv:2611.05686v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We translate the spectral gap-closing criterion for multi-dimensional monotone quasiperiodic Schr\"odinger operators into a concrete dynamical protocol and verify it by large-scale numerics. For a non-principal label we construct a sampling function whose leading eigenfunction weight at the origin vanishes; a local bump then drives the residual weight through zero. The height of a weighted oscillatory time average of the origin-to-localization-center correlator exhibits a deep minimum precisely at the closing, while the site-control label remains featureless and orders of magnitude larger. The signature is robust and maps directly onto superconducting-circuit and photonic platforms.
item.dc:creator: Leonid Parnovski, Roman Shterenberg

item.title: Exact Mirror-Parity Selection Rule for Electron-Phonon Coupling in Two-Dimensional Crystals
item.description:
arXiv:2611.05710v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The electron--phonon (e-ph) interaction underlies conventional superconductivity and plays a central role in transport and other many-body phenomena in solids. Here, we derive a symmetry selection rule for e-ph scattering in two-dimensional crystals possessing a horizontal mirror plane, $\sigma_h$. For electronic states of mirror parity $s_n(\mathbf{k})$ and $s_m(\mathbf{k}+\mathbf{q})$, and a phonon mode of parity $\chi_
u(\mathbf{q})$, we show that the e-ph matrix element $g_{mn,
u}(\mathbf{k},\mathbf{q})$ vanishes identically unless $s_n(\mathbf{k})\,\chi_
u(\mathbf{q})\, s_m(\mathbf{k}+\mathbf{q})=+1$. The rule follows from the covariance of the phonon-induced deformation potential under $\sigma_h$, constitutes the $C_s$ case of the general group-theoretical selection rule for matrix elements, and partitions the e-ph interaction throughout the Brillouin zone into symmetry-allowed and symmetry-forbidden scattering channels. Consequently, mirror-even phonons couple electronic states of the same mirror parity, either even--even or odd--odd, whereas mirror-odd phonons couple only states of opposite mirror parity, for both intra- and interband processes. We illustrate the selection rule through first-principles calculations for the two-dimensional superconductor $\mathrm{Sc_2BCH_4}$, where mirror parity is well defined throughout the entire Brillouin zone and symmetry-forbidden matrix elements vanish up to numerical precision. We then extend the analysis to bulk $\mathrm{MgB_2}$, where the rule applies exactly only on mirror-invariant planes of the three-dimensional Brillouin zone. Moving away from these planes removes the exact mirror constraint and activates scattering channels that are symmetry forbidden when the mirror eigenvalues are well defined. Our results establish horizontal mirror symmetry as an exact and practical filter of e-ph scattering processes.
item.dc:creator: Nicol\'as F. Barrera, Javiera Cabezas-Escares, Francisco Munoz, Carlos Cardenas, Julia Contreras-Garc\'ia

item.title: Static and dynamical Casimir effects in a wedge within the worldline formulation
item.description: arXiv:2611.05768v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study a real massless scalar field in $d+1$ dimensions confined to a wedge of opening angle $\alpha$, in the presence of a semitransparent circular arc that may oscillate radially. Within the worldline formulation, and for an arbitrary strength $\lambda$ of the $\delta$-potential that models the arc, we expand the effective action in powers of the radial displacement $R$ of the arc. In this formulation, all the information about the media is contained in the propagator of a non-relativistic point particle, so that known results for that propagator can be used directly. At zeroth order we obtain the Casimir energy of the wedge, with Dirichlet, Neumann or mixed walls, and the contribution of the arc in closed form for arbitrary $\lambda$. We show that the worldline integrand is, point by point, the energy density obtained from the energy-momentum tensor of the scalar field with curvature coupling $\xi=1/4$; with this identification, and using dimensional regularization for the integrated quantities, we recover the known results for the wedge and for the wedge closed by a Dirichlet arc. At second order in $R$, we reduce the form factor that determines the imaginary part of the in-out effective action, and hence the probability of pair creation by the moving arc, to a one-loop expression involving the radial Green's functions of each angular sector. In the narrow-wedge limit, each angular sector behaves as a field with a mass set by the angular quantization, coupled to a moving $\delta$-mirror; for a Dirichlet arc, the pair creation spectrum of the exterior region approaches that of a planar massive mirror, while the interior region behaves as a tapered cavity. Finally, by decomposing the electromagnetic field into TE and TM scalars, we obtain the Casimir energy of wedges with perfectly conducting, perfectly permeable and mixed walls.
item.dc:creator: C\'esar Daniel Fosco, Bruno Cardin Guntsche

item.title: Exact teleportation bounds for fermionic Hawking thermality beyond the single-mode approximation
item.description: arXiv:2611.05773v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Fermionic teleportation near a Schwarzschild horizon involves two physically distinct ingredients that are often varied together: Hawking thermal mixing and the relative composition of the right and left Unruh modes. We separate them by factorizing the reduced map of the detected exterior fermionic mode into a mode-preparation channel and a Hawking thermal channel. At fixed right-left Unruh-mode composition, we then solve a global constrained quantum-channel optimization over all two-qubit resource states whose fully entangled fraction remains at or below the standard teleportation threshold immediately before thermal mixing. A parity twirl and positivity reduce the arbitrary-state problem exactly to a two-variable quadratic optimization. The solution yields a necessary-and-sufficient activation boundary, a second exact boundary for attaining the universal optimum, and explicit optimizing states. The resulting phase diagram contains a strict no-go region, a composition-limited activation region, and a universal-bound region. The analysis converts state-specific observations of Hawking-assisted teleportation into exact channel-level bounds over the full two-qubit state space.
item.dc:creator: Zhiming Huang

item.title: Coherence Spreading Law in Quenched Homogeneous Bose Gases
item.description: arXiv:2611.05775v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We investigate nonequilibrium coherence spreading in quenched homogeneous bosonic gases both analytically and numerically. Our ensemble-averaged Gross-Pitaevskii trajectory approach and kinetic analysis confirm the linear-in-time growth of the squared coherence length, and explicitly give the spreading-law dependence on the ratio of initial energy to healing energy. When the ratio is relatively small, the squared coherence length grows at a universal rate determined by the ratio of Planck's constant to the particle mass, insensitive to interaction strength and initial momentum distributions. However, our further calculations uncover fundamental limitations to such universality and establish its phase boundaries governed by low system energies, weak interparticle interactions and many-body integrability. Our theory fully reproduces the key experimental signatures and resolves the puzzle of the dynamical origin of the recently observed universal coherence-spreading speed limit [Nature 647, 608-612 (2025)]. Going beyond existing experimental observations, we provide some testable predictions for ultracold-atom experiments and clarify the conditions for the emergence of universal coherent dynamics in nonequilibrium bosonic many-body systems.
item.dc:creator: Yi Cao, Li-Chen Zhao, Jie Liu

item.title: Emergent Incompressibility in Polariton Condensates for Scalable XY Spin Simulation
item.description: arXiv:2611.05782v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Driven-dissipative polariton networks offer a powerful analog platform for simulating continuous-spin Hamiltonians. However, their practical scalability is fundamentally limited by amplitude-phase coupling and metastable trapping in highly frustrated energy landscapes. Here, we present an \textit{in situ} dual-enhancement mechanism to address these bottlenecks without requiring external site-specific fine-tuning. First, a renormalization-group analysis based on density rescaling shows that higher-order nonlinear loss drives the condensates toward an incompressible regime, intrinsically suppressing amplitude fluctuations and enforcing phase-only dynamics. For macroscopic XY networks (up to 10,000 spins), this phase-amplitude decoupling yields a more than 50-fold reduction in energy, while simultaneously shrinking the standard deviation by a factor of six. More generally, it restores the extensive scaling of the optimized XY energy with system size. Second, to navigate the rugged, nonconvex energy landscape, we introduce weak Hermitian pulses. When implemented through a multistage protocol, these pulses enable repeated escapes from local minima and drive the system to deeper energy minima. Benchmarking shows an increasing advantage with system size, with the polariton simulator outperforming the classical Monte Carlo-SQP baseline in every sampled macroscopic realization. Our work provides a physical framework for scalable polariton analog computing.
item.dc:creator: Chengyong Yu, Youya Xu, Xuan Ye, Yan Zhou, Sanjib Ghosh

item.title: Analytic two-body density-matrix spectrum of the Fermionic Tonks-Girardeau gas
item.description: arXiv:2611.05820v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The two-body density matrix (TBDM) of a quantum many-body system provides information about particle correlations, e.g., pairing. In this work, we derive the complete spectrum of the TBDM of the fermionic Tonks-Girardeau gas using its exact ground-state wavefunction in second quantization. We obtain analytical expressions for all eigenvalues and eigenvectors for an arbitrary number of particles and identify two different types of eigenstates: collective states, formed by superpositions of paired momentum modes, and single-determinant states. We provide a physical interpretation of this structure, explaining the origin of the different eigenstates and their degeneracies. We further derive an asymptotic expansion for the largest eigenvalue, improving on previous estimates and analytically confirming its linear scaling with the particle number, thereby indicating off-diagonal long-range order. For the high-index collective states, we obtain simpler expressions for the eigenvalues and eigenvectors, showing that the eigenvalues decay as $n^{-4}$ and that the eigenvectors become independent of the number of particles. Finally, we discuss the connection between the collective states and an effective description in terms of composite bosons, whose spectral properties suggest a behavior consistent with Tan's contact for interacting bosonic systems.
item.dc:creator: Abel Rojo-Franc\`{a}s, Joan Martorell, Francesc Sabater, Bruno Juli\'{a}-D\'{i}az

item.title: Magnetic Bloch eigenvalue problems in nonuniform periodic magnetic fields: a Fourier-finite difference approach
item.description: arXiv:2611.05950v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study magnetic Bloch eigenvalue problems for two-dimensional magnetic Schr\"odinger operators with nonuniform periodic magnetic fields and periodic scalar potentials, and develop a hybrid Fourier-finite difference discretization. A Landau-type gauge is constructed by solving a periodic Poisson equation. Under the integer magnetic flux condition, the magnetic Bloch boundary conditions are incorporated through shifts of Fourier-mode indices. The method combines link-variable-based covariant central differences in the $x$-direction with a Fourier pseudospectral discretization in the $y$-direction, yielding a Hermitian discrete Hamiltonian. The resulting eigenvalue problems are solved using a LOBPCG method. Under appropriate regularity assumptions, we establish a fully discrete consistency residual estimate of order $O(h_1^2+N_2^{-s})$. With suitable spectral separation and eigenspace dimension-preserving conditions, error estimates of the same order are derived for isolated eigenvalues and their associated eigenspaces. Numerical experiments show second-order convergence in the finite difference direction and rapid error reduction with increasing Fourier resolution, and illustrate band degeneracies and eigenstate distributions in nonuniform periodic magnetic fields.
item.dc:creator: Xueyang Li, Yuanwei Lai

item.title: Quantum Computing for Entanglement Asymmetry and the Quantum Mpemba Effect in Field Theory
item.description: arXiv:2611.05987v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We construct a quantum measurement protocol for estimating the R\'enyi entanglement asymmetry, which quantifies symmetry breaking at the level of a subsystem and provides a probe of the quantum Mpemba effect. The protocol combines the SWAP test with a charge-resolving procedure based on randomized symmetry rotations. For a fixed additive accuracy $\epsilon$, the required number of measurements scales as $\mathcal{O}(\epsilon^{-2})$ without explicit dependence on the total system size, making the protocol particularly attractive for quantum many-body systems and lattice quantum field theories. As a representative application, we study the quantum Mpemba effect in the lattice Schwinger model with a $\theta$ term using classical state-vector simulations. We further estimate the resources required to implement the protocol on noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) devices, fault-tolerant quantum computers (FTQCs), and a representative early-FTQC architecture. Our results provide a measurement-efficient framework for investigating anomalous symmetry-restoration dynamics in quantum many-body systems and quantum field theories.
item.dc:creator: Keisuke Fujii, Harunobu Fujimura, Masazumi Honda, Duc Truyen Le

item.title: Statistical mechanics and hierarchy of learnability in quantum codes: From generalized symmetries to non-Abelian topological orders
item.description: arXiv:2611.06154v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Local weak measurements provide noisy information about observables encoded in a quantum code. We formulate the corresponding Bayesian inference problem for a broad class of topological stabilizer codes by mapping it to classical spin models with generalized symmetries. When the wavefunction deformation and Gaussian measurement strengths coincide, the replicated model acquires an enlarged symmetry. We use this symmetry to derive exact identities among correlators averaged over measurement records that quantify the learnability of nonlocal observables associated with fractionalized excitations. Together with correlation inequalities in the associated clean ferromagnetic models, these identities establish hierarchies of learnability: if two observables remain learnable at long distances, their product must also remain learnable. We demonstrate these relations in the rank-2 toric code and the X-cube model, whose classical descriptions exhibit modulated and subsystem symmetries, respectively. We further extend the analysis to finite group quantum double models, including non-Abelian ones. We derive exact relations between learnability and correlations in the corresponding classical models, and show that the representation structure and fusion rules of anyons impose further constraints under suitable positivity conditions. These results constrain which types of nonlocal information can be learned simultaneously, providing a guide to learning phase diagrams in quantum codes under local weak measurements.
item.dc:creator: Hiromi Ebisu, Masazumi Honda

item.title: Hyperbolic Nanocavities for Single-Molecule Vibrational Strong Coupling
item.description: arXiv:2611.06240v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Hyperbolic phonon polaritons (HPhPs) in low-loss anisotropic materials such as hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) provide extreme sub-diffractional field confinement in the mid-infrared, making them attractive for enhancing the interaction of light with molecular vibrations. Collective vibrational strong coupling between molecular ensembles and HPhPs has already been demonstrated in extended slabs. Reaching this regime with a single molecule, however, remains a major challenge, and would provide a platform for investigating how vacuum electromagnetic fields influence molecular dynamics and chemical reactivity. Here, we show theoretically that single-molecule vibrational strong coupling can be reached in hBN nanocavities that laterally confine HPhPs within a finite volume. Combining full-wave electromagnetic simulations with the few-mode quantization approach, we find that these nanocavities support a rich set of asymmetric resonances that strongly enhance the local spectral density, with frequencies that follow from simple HPhP ray trajectories and can be tuned through the cavity aspect ratio. We identify resonances with quality factors of about $600$ and effective mode volumes of $|V_{\mathrm{eff}}| \sim 10^{-7}\lambda^{3}$, sufficient for single-molecule strong coupling with vibrational transitions with dipole moments on the order of $1\,\mathrm{D}$. These results establish hyperbolic nanocavities as a promising platform for single-molecule vibrational strong coupling and open new routes toward the local control of vibrational dynamics and molecular energy flow.
item.dc:creator: Stavros Athanasiou, Olivier J. F. Martin, Francisco J. Garc\'ia-Vidal, Johannes Feist

item.title: Kardar--Parisi--Zhang density hydrodynamics in a coherent XXZ--ASEP Lindbladian
item.description: arXiv:2611.06369v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Coherent interactions can generate quantum correlations without changing a stationary density current. Whether that current still determines long-wavelength transport is a dynamical question. We study an XXZ chain with asymmetric Lindblad hopping, whose stationary current has the asymmetric simple exclusion process (ASEP) form although its populations do not evolve autonomously. The current curvature and static susceptibility fix the leading Kardar--Parisi--Zhang (KPZ) length and amplitude without a fitted length or amplitude conversion factor. The density-visible Liouvillian spectrum, real-space spreading, and Fourier relaxation support KPZ scaling at the finite coherent couplings studied. Central and intermediate stationary density correlations are consistent with the Pr\"ahofer--Spohn profile at this microscopic scale, with resolved finite-time corrections. Reservoir-matched classical references quantify boundary effects, while symmetric hopping recovers diffusion and reduced asymmetry produces the expected crossover. These results connect an exact nonlinear current to the observed long-wavelength KPZ transport of the physical density in an interacting open quantum chain away from the isotropic Heisenberg point.
item.dc:creator: Yansheng Liu, Daoguang Li, Kaixiang Lu, Mingdi Xu, Lei Pan

item.title: Constraining Lorentz Invariance Violation via Precision Atomic Spectroscopy
item.description: arXiv:2611.06392v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This paper investigates Lorentz violation arising from quantum gravity effects in electronic and muonic hydrogen atoms. The violation is modeled through a modified dispersion relation parameterized by a dimensionless coefficient $\xi$ and suppressed by the Planck scale. Using high-precision spectroscopic data and a chi-squared fitting procedure that carefully accounts for theoretical uncertainties in the Rydberg constant and the proton radius, the analysis yields a 95% confidence level constraint $\xi \in [-14.3,\; 1.37] \times 10^5$. The mass scaling of the effect reveals two distinct regimes: for the lowest-order deformation, the heavy nucleus amplifies the signal, while for higher-order corrections, the lepton dominates the sensitivity. These bounds approach Planck-scale sensitivity using the simplest atomic systems, thereby circumventing ambiguities inherent in more complex quantum systems.
item.dc:creator: A. S. Lemos, J. E. J. Matias, F. Dahia, I. P. Lobo

item.title: Quasi-Normal Modes and thermalization in integrable Quantum Field Theories from the Thermodynamic Bethe Ansatz
item.description: arXiv:2611.06473v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We propose a Thermodynamic Bethe Ansatz (TBA) approach for describing thermalization in integrable quantum field theories. The exponential damping and oscillations when approaching thermal equilibrium can be understood as the analogs of quasi-normal mode (QNM) frequencies of black hole perturbations within the framework of holography. Holographic intuitions and some general properties of thermal Green's functions motivate the existence of such a TBA formulation, as well as lead to the imposition of a nonstandard analytical structure on the QNM TBA, while comparison with integrable form-factor expansions fixes the remaining ingredients. We conjecture the QNM TBA to be equivalent to performing an all-order resummation of secular terms in a thermal form factor expansion of retarded 2-point correlation functions. We compare the predictions with tensor network simulations of the E8 deformation of Ising CFT at nonzero temperature. We conjecture that the QNM TBA framework should also be applicable for describing out-of-equilibrium approach to Generalized Hydrodynamics (GHD).
item.dc:creator: Zoltan Bajnok, Romuald A. Janik

item.title: Stability of energy gap of macroscopic quantum matter
item.description: arXiv:2611.06528v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In quantum many-body physics and quantum field theory, it is often assumed that gapped systems remain gapped under sufficiently weak local perturbations. However, to what extent this assumption holds is elusive, except for some special systems. In this work, we examine the stability of energy gap of macroscopic quantum matter that is only subject to two physically natural conditions, locality and translation invariance. We first show that in any spatial dimension, there are gapped local Hamiltonians with a unique ground state and an unstable gap, i.e., they become gapless under certain arbitrarily weak local perturbation in the thermodynamic limit. We then prove that for both spin and fermionic systems in one dimension, such Hamiltonians with an unstable gap must not only break translation invariance but also be fine-tuned. We further show that in any dimension greater than one, there are fine-tuned local translation invariant Hamiltonians with a unique ground state and an unstable gap. These results greatly sharpen our understanding of the fundamental problem of the stability of quantum phases of matter. We also discuss implications of our results on, for example, anyon superconductivity and higher-form symmetries.
item.dc:creator: Kangle Li, Liujun Zou

item.title: A Tensor-Network Chebyshev--Galerkin Method for Boundary-Value Problems in Computational Mechanics
item.description: arXiv:2611.06552v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Quantum-inspired numerical methods for partial differential equations represent discretized fields and operators as quantics tensor trains (QTT), so that their cost depends on how compressible the problem is rather than on the number of unknowns. Global spectral formulations in this setting have so far relied on Fourier bases, restricted to periodic problems, or on collocation, which does not preserve the variational structure exploited by tensor-network solvers. We introduce a QTT Chebyshev--Galerkin method that assembles and solves global spectral systems directly in compressed form, without forming the underlying arrays. Starting from the weak formulation, the method handles coupled elliptic systems with variable coefficients, smoothly mapped geometries, and mixed Dirichlet--Robin boundary conditions, and yields symmetric positive-definite systems suited to variational tensor-network solvers. Parameters and random inputs enter as additional coordinates, so the same construction returns the solution over an entire parameter space in a single solve. In linear elasticity, the method retains spectral convergence and reaches errors below $10^{-8}$ on a three-dimensional benchmark, beyond those attained by QTT finite differences and Q2/Q4 FEniCSx finite elements over the tested range. A six-parameter cantilever design study covering $1.7\times10^{7}$ designs is solved in a single 92~s run, and a stochastic problem with ten random coordinates is represented with $2.4\times10^{6}$ times less memory than its full coefficient array.
item.dc:creator: Juan Jos\'e Rodr\'iguez-Aldavero, \'Angel de la Rosa Velasco, Juan Jos\'e Garc\'ia-Ripoll

item.title: Spectral properties of twisted soft waveguides
item.description: arXiv:2611.06558v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We discuss a model of a soft waveguide described by Schr\"{o}dinger operator whose potential is a twisted straight channel of non-circular profile. We show that a compactly supported twist makes the operator subcritical, the property being expressed in terms of a Hardy-type inequality. On the other hand, a periodic twist raises the essential spectrum and its local slowdown may give rise to isolated eigenvalues below the essential spectrum threshold.
item.dc:creator: Pavel Exner, David Spitzkopf

item.title: Thermodynamics-Informed Learning Captures Hierarchical Hydrogen-Bond Networks in Deep Eutectic Solvents
item.description: arXiv:2611.06590v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Deep eutectic solvents (DESs) offer a tunable platform for lignocellulose refining, but their solvation behavior depends on multicomponent hydrogen-bond networks rather than individual constituent properties. We develop TiNN, a thermodynamics-informed neural network that hierarchically represents HBA-HBD association and solute accommodation through a learned free-energy pathway. Trained on 938 records, TiNN achieves a test-set $R^2$ of 0.917 and generalizes to new HBA-HBD combinations and sparse conditions. Ablation identifies solute-specific stabilization as the largest contributor to prediction accuracy, while the importance of hydrogen-bond compatibility depends on the dissolution mechanism. Experimental measurements of glucose, xylan, and Kraft lignin in acidic, basic, and neutral DESs show that TiNN reduces the geometric mean solubility error from more than 23-fold with COSMO-RS to approximately 1.5-fold. Without training on fractionation data, TiNN also distinguishes DES formulations with high and low lignin and hemicellulose removal from corn stover. These results support chemically grounded solvent screening for lignocellulose fractionation.
item.dc:creator: Yanpeng Ye, Chaoran Duan, Mian Xu, S. Mani Sarathy

item.title: Cryogenic suppression of correlated loss in Rydberg atom arrays
item.description: arXiv:2611.06613v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Blackbody radiation (BBR) poses a central challenge for quantum science with Rydberg atoms. By driving transitions to nearby opposite-parity states, BBR shortens Rydberg lifetimes and has long been suspected to trigger "avalanche" events known to cause correlated atom loss.
